@R44VC0RP Thanks for quick response! I think it’s related to the oc_locale cookie. If you check Chrome DevTools → Application → Cookies: When oc_locale=en, the language selector works fine. So basically, if oc_locale is not en, I’m unable to view the English docs. It seems like the cookie is forcing a redirect back to the current locale when trying to switch to English.

In opencode `v1.2.7` the file type check is no longer using Bun's File I/O, but the lookup function from the `mime-types` library. This function **does not** check if the files exits and just matches the file extension, meaning that the issue persists - pasting strings with image extensions does not work.

The proposed fix is still viable. In `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/component/prompt/index.tsx`, before any mime type checking is done (line 937) a check if the file exists and throwing an exception if it does not, fixes the problem.

> 好吧，我彻底解决了面包 termux 兼容性的问题。
> 
> Termux 使用 Bionic（Android 的 libc），但 Bun 是基于 glibc 编译的。标准的变通方法是使用 grun（glibc-runner），但这会破坏 Bun 捆绑的可执行文件，因为 /proc/self/exe 指向的是 ld.so，而不是实际的二进制文件。
> 
> Bun捆绑的可执行文件通过读取/proc/self/exe并寻找---- Bun！ 来检测其嵌入的JavaScript！----魔法预告片。当 /proc/self/exe 指向 ld.so 时，Bun 找不到其嵌入代码，会退回到 CLI 模式。
> 
> ## 解决方案
> 该工具使用 userland exec——它通过 mmap（） 加载 glibc 的 ld.so，直接跳转到 execve（）。由于内核只在 execve（） 上更新 /proc/self/exe，它仍然指向包含嵌入 JavaScript 的二进制文件。
> 
> 我用 C 语言写了一个自定义的用户空间执行封装。现在 Opencode、Droid、Claude 代码和 Amp 都能在 termux 上原生运行。Opencode 有点复杂，因为它从 $bunfs 加载 OpenTui，而 termux 上没有，所以我加了一个 dlopen 拦截来调用$bunfs，现在 Opencode 可以正常运行了
> 
> 这是带源代码的仓库：https://github.com/kaan-escober/bun-termux-loader

A very powerful solution👍 I think we can close the problem completely.

**#7876** describes the same root cause — `external_directory` permission defaulting to `"ask"` and hanging in headless mode. This issue adds a specific trigger scenario: the `realpath` vs `process.cwd()` symlink mismatch in the bash tool causes files that are *inside* the project to appear "outside" it, triggering the `external_directory` check unexpectedly. This happens on macOS (`/tmp` → `/private/tmp`) and with any symlinked project directories.

**#13715** is related but broader (nested subagent sessions). The underlying problem is the same: `"ask"` has no fallback in contexts without a UI responder.

Happy to close this as a duplicate of #7876 if the symlink mismatch detail is captured there. The two issues are:
1. `"ask"` hanging in headless mode (same as #7876)
2. `Instance.directory` not being `realpath`-resolved, causing false `external_directory` triggers (new detail)

For anyone hitting this on Alacritty, adding this to your `~/.config/alacritty/alacritty.toml` fixes it:


```
[[keyboard.bindings]]
key = "Return"
mods = "Shift"
chars = "\u001b[13;2u"
```
This forces Alacritty to emit the Kitty keyboard protocol sequence for Shift+Enter. Restart Alacritty after applying.

Qwen3-Coder-Next produces duplicate `filePath` parameters for some write tool calls. This breaks the streaming logic in llama.cpp because it didn't account for the possibility of the same key appearing twice. That's a reasonable assumption for models with well-behaved output but for some reason Qwen3-Coder-Next will emit multiple `filePath` parameters some times.

This explains why disabling streaming was a workaround.

I made a minimal PR for llama.cpp to support duplicate tool call parameter keys: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/19753

This patch resolves the problems I was seeing with write tool calls that had an extra malformed `filePath` at the end.

If anyone can capture the failing tool calls for other cases I'll take a look at those too.
